# Cosimo by Medici & Company

> Financial operations software for banks, funds, insurance teams, and financial services firms.

Cosimo is an AI agent for financial operations from Medici & Company. It prepares reports, checks, follow-ups, and review packs from existing records. The homepage routes visitors to banks (/banks/), funds (/funds/), insurance (/insurance/), and financial services (/services/). Each process is configured and tested with the team responsible for it.

## How a process is set up

Start with the records behind one recurring task and an example of the output the team needs. Medici & Company configures and tests the process with the team, using its source records, reporting format, and approval requirements. Drafts bring figures and commentary together, with missing information and open questions marked for review. The team checks the work, resolves questions, and approves the final version.

The FAQ identifies Google Drive, SharePoint, Gmail, Outlook, and Google Calendar connections. Task-specific setup and testing are required. An evaluation can begin with agreed file exports; connections to core banking, policy, claims, or accounting systems require a separate scope review. Cosimo does not currently have a SOC 2 report; a SOC 2 examination is on the roadmap. Data handling, access, retention, scope, and commercial terms are reviewed before starting.

## Banks

Path: /banks/

Loan activity reviews, borrower review packs, account-file checks, and review preparation are starting points for bank operations teams. The fictional Cabini Bank example contains a four-page morning review and inspectable source excerpts. It identifies a possible duplicate repayment, a difference from an independent closing balance, and an outstanding borrower certificate. The duplicate remains a question for the bank to resolve; the example does not post adjustments or make lending decisions.

## Fund overview

Path: /funds/

The fund overview introduces three recurring jobs: investor reporting, portfolio updates, and investor requests. An interactive example follows management accounts, company commentary, and a prior report format into a quarterly portfolio update.

The example uses Chianti Capital, the synthetic demo manager. Six companies report $70.0 million in quarterly revenue against a $72.0 million budget. Calderwood's accounts show $9.0 million while its management update says $9.4 million. The draft uses the accounts provisionally and leaves the $400,000 difference visible for review. The example has inspectable source records and a three-page draft. It is authored demonstration content, not a live application run.

## Insurance

Path: /insurance/

Renewal preparation, submission checks, claims-file summaries, and document follow-ups are starting points for insurance teams. The fictional Lanterna Insurance example contains a four-page operations review and inspectable source excerpts. It follows missing renewal documents, conflicting declared cargo values, and an incomplete claims file. Underwriting, pricing, coverage, and claims decisions remain with the responsible professionals.

## Financial Services

Path: /services/

Administration, accounting, and advisory firms can start with client reporting, document collection, and review packs. Each process is configured around the firm's source records, reporting format, and review requirements. The responsible professionals retain client advice and sign-off.

## Real estate

Path: /re/

The page focuses on quarterly LP reports, investor statements, capital call notices, and distribution notices. The reporting example uses property figures, manager updates, and investor capital records for fictional Loggia Property Group. Visitors can compare source records with the proposed draft and explore a six-page sample report.

The example preserves open property questions and shows a simplified capital-movement schedule. That schedule excludes income and valuation changes and is not a complete capital account statement. Investor notices use supplied, approved allocations; they do not execute payments.

## Venture capital

Path: /vc/

The page focuses on preparing portfolio and LP updates from founder submissions, company spreadsheets, and fund records. Its fictional Telescope Ventures example contains six companies, five current submissions, one stale submission, and a company with six months of runway at its reported burn rate. An unsigned financing discussion is not treated as cash received.

The six-page example includes portfolio metrics, cash and runway, founder commentary, capital movements, and open items. Company operating figures are not fund performance or valuation measures. The sample capital schedule is incomplete until the necessary approved allocations and adjustments are included.

## Private equity

Path: /pe/

The page focuses on bringing portfolio-company financials, management commentary, and fund records into reporting drafts. Its fictional Chianti Capital example compares company actuals with budgets and explains an EBITDA shortfall from supplied management notes. Unexplained variances and unapproved operating plans remain visible.

The six-page sample includes portfolio metrics, budget comparisons, company updates, capital movements, and review questions. The company totals are management-reported operating figures, not ownership-weighted fund results. The sample does not implement an ILPA reporting template or constitute a complete quarterly financial reporting package.

## Private credit

Path: /credit/

The page focuses on private credit and direct lending: borrower review packs, covenant worksheets, reporting follow-ups, and LP updates. Its fictional Fiorino Debt Partners example follows six loans through servicing data, supplied covenant calculations, and a reporting tracker.

One worksheet shows leverage of 4.80 times using submitted EBITDA and 5.33 times if an unresolved add-back is excluded, compared with a supplied maximum of 5.00 times. This is a review question, not a determination of compliance or default. Another item identifies a missing borrower certificate. Cash interest received and PIK accrued are shown separately; neither is presented as the fund's net return.

The six-page credit pack is an authored example. Agreement definitions, adjustments, testing dates, and exceptions require the credit team's review. Lending decisions remain with the team.

## Hedge funds

Path: /hedge/

The page focuses on investor letters, close-file exceptions, subscription/redemption activity, and allocator response drafts. Its fictional Anamorphic Capital example uses administrator-approved figures and supplied policy records for a long/short equity fund.

The six-page monthly pack separates investor-facing drafts from internal working papers. It includes class returns, an exposure snapshot, investor activity, a cash discrepancy, and a questionnaire response that needs current supporting evidence. The example uses administrator-approved figures. The fund team resolves exceptions and approves investor communications, with valuation and sign-off responsibilities retained under its agreed arrangements. The page does not claim to perform trading, investment decisions, complete risk management, or independent assurance.

## About the examples

All interactive demonstrations use fictional records and prepared outputs. Interactions let visitors inspect the proposed document workflow, source records, figures, and review questions. They are not recordings of Cosimo generating these outputs, successful production proof runs, or customer results.

The examples explain the intended work. They do not substantiate a guaranteed processing time, hours saved, universal accuracy, autonomous delivery, audit readiness, or integration coverage. Each process needs configuration and testing with the team responsible for it.

## How to start

Email info@medici.ai with a few sentences about the report or process your team prepares, where the information comes from, and which part takes the most time. Medici & Company will work through a first workflow to test with the team. Scope, data requirements, an NDA, and commercial terms are agreed before source files are shared. An evaluation uses agreed source records, written feasibility confirmation, and a review of the output against its sources. Model usage is charged at cost without markup; platform terms are agreed in conversation.

## Customer fit and responsibilities

Cosimo is for banks, funds, insurance teams, and financial services firms with recurring manual work. Fit depends on the specific process, records, and review requirements. Cosimo supports operations teams alongside their systems and advisers. For funds, it is not the administrator of record. Accounting, valuation, lending, investment, underwriting, claims decisions, and professional sign-off remain with the responsible people. Client data is restricted to that client’s work and is not used to train shared models.

## Tested product work

Clients use Cosimo daily. In an internal test on a synthetic real estate fund with five properties and eight investors, Cosimo matched every report figure to the cent against an 88-row source sheet and raised five exceptions for review. This work is separate from the illustrative website walkthroughs. Acceptance criteria are agreed for each client evaluation. Approval rules are configurable per process and user; the product can send authorized communications.
